artifact: S2 post-merge gate — /api/meta git_sha tracks redeploys — RAN
why_this_exists: S2 (PR #31, merged e6810a4 2026-08-22) carried one UNRUN gate that no agent could run from inside a session: the deployed sha has to be observed MOVING across two redeploys, not merely existing (ADR-028 §g, PR #31 R9). Under ADR-022 rule 2 the row cannot archive to DONE.md while that gate is UNRUN. This file is the observation record; it makes no claim beyond the HTTP responses listed.
gate_text_verbatim: `/api/meta` reports a real sha **that tracks redeploys** — **UNRUN**, and unrunnable from here: no agent can run a Zeabur build, so this is confirmed by `curl -s https://whaleforce-sec10k.zeabur.app/api/meta` after the merge and again after a second redeploy — **the sha must MOVE across two redeploys, not merely exist**, which is the only observation that catches a cached build layer freezing a real-but-stale sha (ADR-028 §g, PR #31 R9).
how_run: Three real HTTP GETs against the deployed instance (no mocks, hard rule 4), each paired with `git log` of the commit the returned sha names. The first two were made by the orchestrator and relayed to the implementer with timestamps; the implementer could not reproduce the 1efc457 response (that build had already been replaced) and re-confirmed the current one itself.

commit_chain_since_pr31_merge.base: e6810a4 2026-08-22T09:42:29Z Merge pull request #31 from HaoweiChan/task/S2 (S2 itself; the build this gate's mechanism first shipped in)
commit_chain_since_pr31_merge.reading: Zeabur rebuilds on every push to main, so each first-parent merge after e6810a4 is a redeploy. What the responses show: two distinct real shas (1efc457e598d at 07:47:22Z, 1ed784ccf68e at 07:49:54Z and 07:51:52Z), each equal to a commit on main's first-parent chain, and ONE move seen at both ends (1efc457 -> 1ed784c, between 07:47:22Z and 07:49:54Z, 152 s apart). The deployed sha was never observed at e6810a4 or 6c71ca6 — the only pre-S2 deployed observation on record is git_sha 'unknown' (2026-08-22) — so e6810a4 -> 1efc457 is inferred from the chain, not seen. The build running at 07:47:22Z was NOT the one merged 87 s earlier (07:45:55Z), so the sha was not reading from a live git checkout of main either — it changed only when the new image came up (1ed784c first seen 239 s after its merge), which is the injected-at-build behaviour ADR-028 §b specifies.

intervals_recomputed.note: PR #36 R1: an earlier version of this record (commit 5a6d718) gave this interval as 92, not 87; corrected 2026-08-23 in round 1.

verdict: RAN — SATISFIED: two distinct real shas observed, one move seen end-to-end — (e6810a4, 6c71ca6: deployed sha not observed) -> 1efc457e598d observed 07:47:22Z -> 1ed784ccf68e observed 07:49:54Z and 07:51:52Z; matches origin/main at observation. The gate's wording (a curl after the merge and again after a second redeploy, the sha must move) is met by the 1efc457 -> 1ed784c move.
not_claimed: No /api/meta response ever showed e6810a4 (the S2 merge itself) or 6c71ca6 (PR #33) as the deployed sha; the only pre-S2 deployed observation on record is git_sha 'unknown' (2026-08-22). Their place in the chain is inferred from git and Zeabur's push-to-main trigger, not observed, so 'e6810a4 -> 1efc457' is not a seen move.
Only ONE move was seen at both ends (1efc457 -> 1ed784c). Two distinct real shas were observed; a second end-to-end move was not.

No observation of a build that FAILED to move: the cached-layer failure mode ADR-028 §g names (a real-but-stale sha frozen by a cached build layer) is excluded only by the one move actually seen, not by any test that would force it to occur.

The implementer did not reproduce the 1efc457 observation — that build was gone by 07:51; the implementer's observation confirms the current sha and the git facts only. The two orchestrator observations are relayed with their timestamps, not re-observed.
No claim about WHEN within the 87-239 s window after the PR #35 merge the new image came up; only that it had not at 07:47:22Z and had by 07:49:54Z.

The first version of this record (commit 5a6d718) gave the PR #35-merge-to-first-observation interval as 92 (it is 87) and presented e6810a4 as an observed chain start; both corrected in PR #36 round 1 (R1, R3).
